profile.summary: gLM2 is a genomic language model that reads a stretch of genome as a mixture of two alphabets: protein coding regions as amino acids, and the intergenic sequence between them as nucleotides. Each element is prefixed with a strand token. It is a transformer encoder trained by masked language modelling on the OMG metagenomic corpus, and the authors say its representations carry functional information as well as coevolutionary signals in protein-protein interfaces and genomic regulatory syntax.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: Model Description; model card: Model Description; Europe PMC abstract

summary_quotes.text: gLM2 is a mixed-modality genomic language model
It encodes a genomic contig as a sequence of protein coding sequences (CDS) and DNA inter-genic sequences (IGS).
CDS elements are tokenized using per-amino acid tokens, and IGS elements are tokenized using per-nucleotide tokens.
we prepended each genomic element with a special token, either `<+>` or `<->` to indicate the positive and negative strands
that leverages genomic context information to learn robust functional representations, as well as coevolutionary signals in protein-protein interfaces and genomic regulatory syntax

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: gLM2 is a transformer encoder trained with the masked language modelling objective: 30% of both amino-acid and nucleotide tokens are masked, and cross-entropy loss is applied only on the masked tokens. The input is a contig written as alternating coding and intergenic elements: coding elements as uppercase amino acids, intergenic elements as lowercase nucleotides, so the two alphabets cannot collide, and each element prefixed by <+> or <-> for the strand. The paper's motivation is that nucleotide-only models need very long contexts for genes, while protein-only genomic models ignore the regulatory sequence between genes. The 650M checkpoint has depth 33, dimension 1280 and 20 heads; the 150M checkpoint has depth 30, dimension 640 and 10 heads; both use RoPE, SwiGLU and RMS normalisation. Both were trained for 600k steps, 315B tokens, with a context length of 4096. An update in September 2024 raised the context from 2048 to 4096 tokens and changed intergenic tokenisation from BPE to per-nucleotide.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two checkpoints are published: tattabio/gLM2_150M and tattabio/gLM2_650M. Both cards carry the same September 2024 update note, the same 315B pretraining tokens and the same 4096 context length, and their configs differ in size: depth 33 and dimension 1280 for 650M, depth 30 and dimension 640 for 150M. A result should name which checkpoint was used and its Hugging Face revision, because the September 2024 update changed both the context length and the intergenic tokenisation. This page read the 650M checkpoint at revision 3c4037ae and the 150M checkpoint at revision 93c88529.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Mixed-modality genomic language model: a transformer encoder trained with masked language modelling over amino-acid and nucleotide tokens.

quotes.text: gLM2 is a transformer encoder trained with the masked language modeling objective.

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Transformer encoder with RoPE position encoding, SwiGLU feed-forward layers and RMS normalisation, using Flash Attention 2. Per the paper's Appendix E: gLM2-150M has dimension 640, 10 heads and 30 layers; gLM2-650M has dimension 1280, 20 heads and 33 layers. The 650M config agrees (depth 33, dimension 1280, 20 heads) and adds a SwiGLU multiple of 256 and a vocabulary of 37.

quotes.text: gLM2 uses RoPE (Su et al., 2023) position encoding, SwiGLU (Shazeer, 2020) feed-forward layers, and RMS normalization (Zhang & Sennrich, 2019).
We leverage Flash Attention 2 (Dao, 2023) to speed up attention computation over the sequence length of 4096.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: A genomic contig as one string: coding sequences as uppercase amino acids, intergenic sequences as lowercase nucleotides, each element prefixed by <+> or <-> for the strand.

facts.value: Per-token embeddings from the last hidden state. The masked language modelling head is available through AutoModelForMaskedLM; the repository also computes a categorical Jacobian from the model to show protein-protein interactions.

facts.label: Training data
facts.value: The OMG (Open MetaGenomic) corpus: 3.1T base pairs and 3.3B protein coding sequences, combining JGI's IMG and EMBL's MGnify, with the databases' own gene predictions. Contigs shorter than 2kb, contigs with fewer than seven elements or three coding sequences, and elements with over 20% invalid characters were removed. Semantic Deduplication at an embedding distance threshold of 2e-3 pruned 49% of it. Both checkpoints were trained on the pruned corpus for 600k steps, 315B pretraining tokens each, with 30% of tokens masked.

facts.label: Context limits
facts.value: 4096 tokens, as stated in the model card and the paper, raised from 2048 in the September 2024 update. One token is one amino acid in a coding region or one nucleotide in an intergenic region. The paper says this window holds 9.7 ± 3.3 coding and intergenic elements per training example.

strengths.text: The authors report that the categorical Jacobian of gLM2_650M on the concatenated ModA and ModC sequences (PDB 2ONK) shows inter-protein contacts that match an MSA-based coevolution model, checked against the PDB structure, where they say ESM2 650M and Evo show none.

quotes.text: gLM2 correctly predicts interactions between 2ONK_A (ModA) and 2ONK_C (ModC).
In comparison, ESM2 and Evo do not predict any interactions.
closely matches the co-evolutionary signal that can be learned from multiple sequence alignment (MSA) based Potts model
Such protein- protein interface signals cannot be extracted in existing language model methods such as ESM2 650M and Evo-1-8k-base
We validate the gLM2-predicted contacts directly with the ground truth contacts from 2ONK PDB structure (Fig. 5).

limitations.text: Input must be prepared, not raw DNA: coding regions have to be called and translated to uppercase amino acids, intergenic sequence kept as lowercase nucleotides, and each element given a strand token. The tokenizer depends on that case and on the strand tokens.

quotes.text: To avoid collision between amino acid and nucleotide tokens, the tokenizer expects all amino acids to be uppercase, and all nucleotides to be lowercase.
# NOTE: Nucleotides should always be lowercase, and prepended with `<+>`.

limitations.text: The context is 4096 tokens, so only a short stretch of a genome fits in one pass. The September 2024 update raised it from 2048 tokens and changed the intergenic tokenisation, so the checkpoint revision matters when reporting a result.

quotes.text: UPDATE(09/2024): We updated the model with longer context length (4096 tokens vs. 2048 tokens) and per-nucleotide IGS tokenization instead of BPE.

limitations.text: The training corpus is metagenomic and, in the paper's words, primarily prokaryotic and viral. The paper says common gene-calling tools fail on eukaryotic sequences and that the corpus uses the databases' own gene predictions, so protein sequences predicted from eukaryotic contigs may be of poor quality.

quotes.text: unstructured metagenomic (primarily prokaryotic and viral) sequences
Many standard metagenomic post-processing steps (e.g. gene calling) fail on eukaryotic sequences, resulting in poor quality protein sequence predictions.
most metagenomic gene-calling software tools are not optimized for eukaryotic ORF prediction
We utilize the gene predictions conducted by the databases

run_guide.summary: Load the gLM2 650M checkpoint and extract embeddings for a short mixed-modality contig.
prerequisites: A CUDA GPU: the published example calls .cuda() and loads the weights in bfloat16. Memory needs are not stated in the sources read.
Code and weights are Apache-2.0 and the checkpoints are not gated.
The input must already be split into coding and intergenic elements, with amino acids uppercase and nucleotides lowercase.

steps.title: Install PyTorch and transformers
steps.explanation: The sources name no install command; this line installs the two packages their usage example imports.

steps.title: Extract embeddings for a contig
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

model = AutoModel.from_pretrained('tattabio/gLM2_650M', torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, trust_remote_code=True).cuda()
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('tattabio/gLM2_650M', trust_remote_code=True)

# A contig with two proteins and an inter-genic sequence.
# NOTE: Nucleotides should always be lowercase, and prepended with `<+>`.
sequence = "<+>MALTKVEKRNRIKRRVRGKISGTQASPRLSVYKSNK<+>aatttaaggaa<->MLGIDNIERVKPGGLELVDRLVAVNRVTKVTKGGRAFGFSAIVVVGNED"

# Tokenize the sequence.
encodings = tokenizer([sequence], return_tensors='pt')

# Extract embeddings.
with torch.no_grad():
    embeddings = model(encodings.input_ids.cuda(), output_hidden_states=True).last_hidden_state
PY
steps.explanation: The model card's example, wrapped in a shell heredoc. For the smaller model use tattabio/gLM2_150M, as the card and README name it.
